docs.text: Security policy ¶ Supported versions ¶ Security fixes target the current main branch. Deployments should use the latest reviewed revision of main ; older revisions and experimental branches do not receive separate security backports. This policy covers the SpamAPI service, dashboard, and WordPress plugin. Reporting a vulnerability ¶ Report suspected SpamAPI vulnerabilities through the private vulnerability reporting form . Sign in to GitHub to submit a report. Reports are private to the reporter and maintainers handling the advisory. Include the affected component and version, impact, reproduction steps, and a minimal proof of concept using synthetic data. Never send live API keys, tokens, payment details, or customer content. Coordinate disclosure with maintainers after a fix is available, and keep exploit details out of public issues and PRs.

docs.text: API reference ¶ Public API ¶ Send requests to https://api.spamapi.de under the base path /api/v1 . Bodies are JSON with Content-Type: application/json , up to 2 MiB. Endpoints marked with a key need your API key in the X-API-Key header; the quickstart shows how to create one. Errors, rate limits and monthly checks are described in Errors and limits . The OpenAPI specification has the complete schemas. Method Path Key Description POST /check Yes Check content for spam POST /submit-spam Yes Report spam that got through POST /submit-ham Yes Report legitimate content that was flagged GET /usage Yes This month's checks GET /sites Yes Sites that used your keys POST /verify-key No Validate a key GET /pricing No Plans and prices The WordPress plugin also uses the shared-model endpoints under /api/v1/training/ ; see the OpenAPI specification and the WordPress guide . Check content ¶ POST /api/v1/check classifies one comment or form submission. The quickstart has a complete request and response. Check request fields ¶ Field Description blog Required. Your site's URL, up to 2,048 bytes. Site statistics are grouped by it. user_ip Required. The visitor's IPv4 or IPv6 address. user_agent The visitor's browser user agent. referrer The page the visitor came from. permalink The page the submission was made on. comment_type The kind of submission, such as comment , contact-form or signup . comment_author The name the visitor entered, up to 255 bytes. comment_author_email The email address the visitor entered, up to 255 bytes. comment_author_url The website the visitor entered. comment_content The text of the comment or message. blog_lang Your site's language, such as en or de_DE . honeypot_field_value The value of a hidden form field that people leave empty. is_test , user_role Force a ham result; see test mode . installation_id Used by the WordPress plugin. Omit it. api_key Optional. If present, it must be the key in the X-API-Key header. comment_date_gmt , blog_charset , honeypot_field_name , recheck_reason Accepted; currently not used. Send the fields you have. More context gives SpamAPI more to go on. Check response fields ¶ Field Description is_spam true if SpamAPI considers the submission spam. score From 0 (ham) to 1 (spam). recommendation allow , review or discard , derived from the score. request_id Identifies the request; also in the X-Request-ID and X-SpamAPI-Request-ID headers. prediction_ref Reference to the stored check. Absent for test values . reasons Optional short notes about the result, for your logs. Their wording can change; don't build logic on them. statistical Optional diagnostics from SpamAPI's shared comment model, for information only. A successful check also returns the X-Usage-Limit , X-Usage-Used and X-Usage-Remaining headers, and X-SpamAPI-Pro-Tip with the recommendation. Report mistakes ¶ POST /api/v1/submit-spam reports spam that got through; POST /api/v1/submit-ham reports legitimate content that was flagged. Both take blog and user_ip (required), user_agent , comment_type , comment_author , comment_author_email , comment_content and optionally api_key , with the same meaning as for checks. Reports don't use checks and are counted in the dashboard's usage history. Both return HTTP 200 : {"status": "ok"} Monthly usage ¶ GET /api/v1/usage returns this month's checks. It doesn't use one. { "reserved": 1, "remaining": 9987, "limit": 10000, "used": 12, "percentage": "0.12", "resets_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z", "throttled": false } limit : checks included in your plan this month; 0 for unlimited plans. used : completed checks this month. reserved : checks in progress. remaining : checks left after used and reserved ; 0 for unlimited plans. percentage : used as a percentage of limit , as a decimal string. resets_at : when the next month's checks start, in UTC. throttled : true once the checks are used up; checks then get 429 . A paid plan's quota applies until its subscription ends, including the rest of a paid period after cancellation; the account then uses the Free quota. Sites ¶ GET /api/v1/sites lists the sites ( blog values) that used your account's keys, most recently seen first. curl "https://api.spamapi.de/api/v1/sites?limit=50&offset=0" \ -H "X-API-Key: $SPAMAPI_KEY" { "sites": [ { "site": "https://example.com", "api_calls": 12, "spam": 2, "ham": 10, "missed_spam": 0, "false_positives": 0, "first_seen": "2026-11-02T09:15:00Z", "last_seen": "2026-11-04T16:40:12Z" } ], "total": 1, "limit": 50, "offset": 0 } limit defaults to 50 and is capped at 100. missed_spam and false_positives are currently always 0 . The dashboard's sites endpoint uses its own response schema. Verify a key ¶ POST /api/v1/verify-key checks a key sent in the body, without the X-API-Key header. The WordPress plugin's Test Connection uses it. It is limited to 10 requests a minute per IP address; to test a key from your own code, GET /api/v1/usage is simpler. {"api_key": "spa_..."} { "valid": true, "plan": "free", "usage": { "reserved": 0, "remaining": 100, "limit": 100, "used": 0, "percentage": "0.00", "resets_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z" } } plan is free , pro , business or enterprise . When SpamAPI's shared comment model accepts contributions, the response also contains training_policy for the WordPress plugin. An unknown, revoked or malformed key, or an account that can't use the API, returns HTTP 200 with: {"valid": false} Plans and prices ¶ GET /api/v1/pricing needs no API key. It lists the Free, Pro, Business and Enterprise plans with their monthly check quotas, and for Pro and Business the Stripe price that Checkout charges: unit_amount in the currency's minor unit (cents), currency , the billing interval and Stripe's tax_behavior ( inclusive , exclusive , or unspecified , which makes no statement about VAT; Checkout shows the final amount). Enterprise has monthly_checks: null (unlimited under its agreement) and purchase: "contact" ; it is never sold through Checkout. quota_period is utc_calendar_month : only metered POST /check requests count, toward the UTC month in which they were admitted, independent of the subscription's billing dates. quota_exceeded is rejected : checks over the quota get HTTP 429 usage_limit_exceeded and are never billed. { "livemode": true, "quota_period": "utc_calendar_month", "quota_exceeded": "rejected", "plans": [ {"id": "free", "name": "Free", "monthly_checks": 100, "purchase": "signup", "price": null}, {"id": "pro", "name": "Pro", "monthly_checks": 10000, "purchase": "checkout", "price": {"currency": "eur", "unit_amount": 900, "interval": "month", "interval_count": 1, "tax_behavior": "unspecified"}}, {"id": "business", "name": "Business", "monthly_checks": 100000, "purchase": "checkout", "price": {"currency": "eur", "unit_amount": 4900, "interval": "month", "interval_count": 1, "tax_behavior": "unspecified"}}, {"id": "enterprise", "name": "Enterprise", "monthly_checks": null, "purchase": "contact", "price": null} ] } Prices are read from Stripe and reused for up to five minutes. If either price cannot be read or is not a fixed recurring amount, the endpoint returns HTTP 503 pricing_unavailable instead of default or outdated prices. Dashboard and auth APIs ¶ The dashboard at https://app.spamapi.de uses the following endpoints. They authenticate with a dashboard session, not an API key, and aren't meant for integrations; use the public API instead. Dashboard API ¶ Base path: /dashboard/api Method Path Description GET /account Get account PATCH /account Initiate email change GET /api-keys List keys POST /api-keys Create key DELETE /api-keys/{id} Delete key GET /usage/summary Usage summary GET /usage/history Usage history GET /sites Sites stats GET /billing/subscription Subscription POST /billing/checkout Checkout session POST /billing/portal Billing portal Authenticate with Authorization: Bearer <session-token> , using the token returned by registration or login. Account responses wrap the current user in user . Changing the account email requires both email and the current password ; the response still contains the current email until confirmation. Creating a key returns HTTP 200 with key (the full credential, shown only once) and api_key (its metadata). Listing keys returns a keys array; deleting a key returns HTTP 204 with no body. Usage history returns a history array with month , spam_checks , spam_detected , ham_detected , submit_spam , and submit_ham . The lookback defaults to six months and is capped at 24. Subscription details are wrapped in subscription . While a canceled subscription remains active, cancel_at gives its scheduled end and status is unchanged; it is absent otherwise. Checkout requires plan , success_url , and cancel_url ; the billing portal requires return_url . Redirect URLs must use the application's origin ( https://app.spamapi.de for the hosted service). Both endpoints return url . Auth API ¶ Base path: /auth Method Path Description POST /register Register POST /login Login POST /logout Logout GET /me Current user POST /verify Verify email POST /confirm-email-change Confirm email change POST /forgot Forgot password POST /reset Reset password Registration returns HTTP 201 ; login returns HTTP 200 . Both return user , token , and session . GET /auth/me returns user and session , and logout returns HTTP 204 with no body. Email verification and email-change confirmation accept token and return user . Forgot-password accepts email and returns HTTP 202 with {"status":"email_sent"} . Reset-password accepts token and new_password and returns the user object directly. Auth handlers return a JSON error string; their rate limiter and the dashboard session middleware can return plain-text errors.

docs.text: Errors and limits ¶ Error responses ¶ The public API ( /api/v1 ) answers errors with an HTTP status and a JSON body. error is a stable code for your program; message explains it for people and can change. curl https://api.spamapi.de/api/v1/check \ -H "X-API-Key: $SPAMAPI_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"blog": "https://example.com"}' { "error": "validation_error", "message": "user IP is required" } Every response has an X-Request-ID header. Include it when you contact support . You can send your own X-Request-ID , up to 128 printable ASCII characters without spaces, to match SpamAPI's logs with yours; it isn't an idempotency key. Check responses also carry the ID in request_id . An error never contains a spam decision. Don't treat an error as allow . Error codes ¶ Status error Endpoints Meaning and what to do 400 invalid_json POST endpoints The body isn't valid JSON. Fix the request. 400 validation_error check, submit-spam, submit-ham A field is missing or invalid; message names it. blog and user_ip are required, and user_ip must be an IPv4 or IPv6 address. Fix the request. 400 missing_api_key verify-key The body has no api_key . 400 invalid_request check, submit-spam, submit-ham The request couldn't be read. Fix the request. 401 missing_api_key Endpoints with an API key The X-API-Key header is missing. 401 invalid_api_key Endpoints with an API key The key is unknown, revoked or malformed, or an api_key in the body differs from the header. Check the key in the dashboard . 403 account_unavailable check, usage The account can't use the API. Contact support. 403 contribution_denied check installation_id isn't registered for this blog . Omit installation_id unless you use the WordPress plugin. 429 rate_limit_exceeded All except pricing Too many requests in a minute. Wait the number of seconds in Retry-After . 429 usage_limit_exceeded check This month's checks are used up. Wait until resets_at from GET /api/v1/usage , or upgrade your plan. 500 detection_error check The check failed and wasn't counted. Retry later. 500 server_error , feedback_error , usage_error , sites_error verify-key, submit-spam, submit-ham, sites SpamAPI couldn't complete the request. Retry later. 500 internal_server_error All An unexpected failure. The body also contains request_id . Retry later. 503 detection_unavailable check Classification is temporarily unavailable or timed out. The check isn't counted. Hold the submission and retry later. 503 quota_unavailable check, verify-key, usage SpamAPI couldn't read or record usage. Retry later. 503 pricing_unavailable pricing Prices can't be read right now. Request bodies over 2 MiB are rejected. Codes beginning with contribution_ from the shared-model endpoints are described in the OpenAPI specification . A retry is a new request. If a check's response was lost, the retry can use a second check. Retry 5xx and 429 responses with a growing delay, not in a tight loop. Rate limits ¶ Endpoints Limit Endpoints with an API key 100 requests a minute per account, shared by all its keys POST /api/v1/verify-key 10 requests a minute per IP address, including dashboard sign-ins from that address GET /api/v1/pricing No rate limit Responses carry the limit's state: X-RateLimit-Limit : requests allowed in the window. X-RateLimit-Remaining : requests left in the window. X-RateLimit-Reset : end of the window as a Unix timestamp. When the limit is reached, the response is 429 rate_limit_exceeded with a Retry-After header in seconds: { "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "message": "Too many requests" } Monthly checks ¶ Each plan includes a number of checks per month: 100 on Free; see plans and prices for the others. All API keys of an account share them. Each successful POST /api/v1/check counts toward the UTC calendar month in which it was made, independent of billing dates. Test values , feedback reports and usage queries don't count. Neither do checks that return an error, except when SpamAPI couldn't confirm whether it recorded the check ( 503 quota_unavailable ); such a check may count. Check responses carry X-Usage-Limit , X-Usage-Used and X-Usage-Remaining headers. GET /api/v1/usage returns the same numbers and when they reset. Once the checks are used up, checks get 429 usage_limit_exceeded until the next month or until you upgrade. Nothing extra is billed. { "error": "usage_limit_exceeded", "message": "Monthly API usage limit exceeded" } Follow your usage on the dashboard's usage page .

docs.text: Endpoints Limit Endpoints with an API key 100 requests a minute per account, shared by all its keys POST /api/v1/verify-key 10 requests a minute per IP address, including dashboard sign-ins from that address GET /api/v1/pricing No rate limit Responses carry the limit's state: X-RateLimit-Limit : requests allowed in the window. X-RateLimit-Remaining : requests left in the window. X-RateLimit-Reset : end of the window as a Unix timestamp. When the limit is reached, the response is 429 rate_limit_exceeded with a Retry-After header in seconds: { "error": "rate_limit_exceeded", "message": "Too many requests" }
docs.title: Rate limits

docs.text: Each plan includes a number of checks per month: 100 on Free; see plans and prices for the others. All API keys of an account share them. Each successful POST /api/v1/check counts toward the UTC calendar month in which it was made, independent of billing dates. Test values , feedback reports and usage queries don't count. Neither do checks that return an error, except when SpamAPI couldn't confirm whether it recorded the check ( 503 quota_unavailable ); such a check may count. Check responses carry X-Usage-Limit , X-Usage-Used and X-Usage-Remaining headers. GET /api/v1/usage returns the same numbers and when they reset. Once the checks are used up, checks get 429 usage_limit_exceeded until the next month or until you upgrade. Nothing extra is billed. { "error": "usage_limit_exceeded", "message": "Monthly API usage limit exceeded" } Follow your usage on the dashboard's usage page .

docs.text: Getting started with the REST API ¶ Check your first comment or form submission in a few minutes: create a free account and an API key, then send a request from the command line. Using WordPress? Follow the WordPress setup instead; it uses the same account and key. API requests go to https://api.spamapi.de . Your account, keys and usage are in the dashboard . Create a free account ¶ Create a free account with a username, email address and password. SpamAPI emails you a verification token; open the link in the email, or paste the token on the verification page. You then land on the dashboard's API keys page. The Free plan includes 100 checks a month and needs no payment details. Create an API key ¶ Open API keys in the dashboard. Enter a name you will recognize, such as the site or app that will use the key, and select Create key . Copy the key, which starts with spa_ , and store it somewhere safe. The dashboard shows it only this once. Check I saved this key and close the dialog. Keep the key on your server and send it in the X-API-Key header. Never put it in code that runs in a visitor's browser. If a key is lost or exposed, revoke it on the API keys page and create a new one. Stripe keys ( sk_live_… , sk_test_… ) are not SpamAPI keys. All keys of an account share its monthly checks. For the commands below, store the key in an environment variable: export SPAMAPI_KEY='spa_...' Check that the key works ¶ curl https://api.spamapi.de/api/v1/usage \ -H "X-API-Key: $SPAMAPI_KEY" A working key returns this month's checks. This request doesn't use one. { "reserved": 0, "remaining": 100, "limit": 100, "used": 0, "percentage": "0.00", "resets_at": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z", "throttled": false } HTTP 401 with invalid_api_key means the key is mistyped, revoked, or not a SpamAPI key; missing_api_key means the header is missing. Check a submission ¶ Send each comment or form submission to POST /api/v1/check before you publish, store or forward it. Only blog , your site's URL, and user_ip , the visitor's IP address, are required. Add the text, author details and user agent you have; the API reference lists every field. curl https://api.spamapi.de/api/v1/check \ -H "X-API-Key: $SPAMAPI_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "blog": "https://example.com", "user_ip": "203.0.113.10", "user_agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64)", "comment_type": "comment", "comment_author": "Watch Deals", "comment_author_email": "deals@example.net", "comment_content": "Cheap replica watches, order now!" }' The response classifies the submission: { "is_spam": true, "score": 0.594, "recommendation": "review", "request_id": "0f6c2a7e-5d1b-4c39-9e8a-2b7d4f1c6a90", "prediction_ref": "5b0e8f3c-9a4d-4e21-8c67-1d2f3a4b5c6d" } Your score can differ. The response can also contain optional fields such as reasons , short notes about the result for your logs; ignore fields you don't use. Each successful check uses one of your monthly checks. Field Meaning is_spam true if SpamAPI considers the submission spam. score From 0 (ham) to 1 (spam). recommendation allow , review or discard ; see below. request_id Identifies the request. Include it when you contact support. prediction_ref Reference to the stored check. Act on the result ¶ Your code decides what happens. SpamAPI doesn't publish or delete anything. recommendation Suggested action allow Publish or deliver the submission as usual. review Hold it for a person to check. discard Reject it or move it to spam. Scores are estimates and some results will be wrong, so keep a way to review held submissions. When the API can't make a decision, it returns an error instead of a result: 503 detection_unavailable : classification is temporarily unavailable. The check isn't counted. Hold the submission and retry later, or let a person review it; don't treat the error as allow . 429 usage_limit_exceeded : this month's checks are used up. Checks resume when the quota resets ( resets_at ) or after you upgrade . 429 rate_limit_exceeded : too many requests in a minute. Wait for the number of seconds in the Retry-After header. Errors and limits lists every error code and what to do. Report mistakes ¶ If a result was wrong, send the same fields to POST /api/v1/submit-spam for spam that got through, or to POST /api/v1/submit-ham for legitimate content that was flagged: curl https://api.spamapi.de/api/v1/submit-ham \ -H "X-API-Key: $SPAMAPI_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "blog": "https://example.com", "user_ip": "198.51.100.7", "comment_author": "Jane Doe", "comment_author_email": "jane@example.com", "comment_content": "Could you send me a quote for a new roof?" }' {"status": "ok"} Reports don't use checks. The dashboard's usage page counts them. Before you go live ¶ Test your integration with test mode values, which skip classification and don't use checks. Follow your monthly checks in the dashboard or with GET /api/v1/usage , and compare plans if you need more. Start from an example in Go , JavaScript , PHP or Python . Keep troubleshooting at hand.

docs.text: Test mode and test values ¶ Use these values to test how your integration handles spam and ham results. SpamAPI answers them with a fixed result, without classifying the content. They need a valid API key and count toward rate limits . They don't use monthly checks and don't appear in usage or site statistics. Once this month's checks are used up, they are rejected with 429 usage_limit_exceeded like any other check. Their responses have no prediction_ref , because no check is stored. Force a spam result ¶ Send one of these values in POST /api/v1/check . Matching ignores letter case. Field Value comment_author spamapi-guaranteed-spam comment_author viagra-test-123 comment_author_email spam@test.spamapi.com comment_author_email akismet-guaranteed-spam@example.com curl https://api.spamapi.de/api/v1/check \ -H "X-API-Key: $SPAMAPI_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "blog": "https://example.com", "user_ip": "203.0.113.10", "comment_author": "spamapi-guaranteed-spam", "comment_content": "Test submission" }' { "is_spam": true, "score": 1, "recommendation": "discard", "reasons": ["guaranteed_spam"], "request_id": "6f1d9c2b-3e4a-4b5c-8d7e-9f0a1b2c3d4e" } Force a ham result ¶ Set is_test to true and user_role to administrator . Both are required; is_test alone doesn't change the result. This takes precedence over the spam values above. curl https://api.spamapi.de/api/v1/check \ -H "X-API-Key: $SPAMAPI_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "blog": "https://example.com", "user_ip": "203.0.113.10", "comment_content": "Test submission", "user_role": "administrator", "is_test": true }' { "is_spam": false, "score": 0, "recommendation": "allow", "request_id": "1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d" } Don't send is_test or user_role from production traffic unless you mean to skip classification. Test the WordPress plugin ¶ Sign out of WordPress, or use a private browser window, and post a comment or submit a supported form with the email address spam@test.spamapi.com . The plugin treats it as spam; see what happens to spam for each form plugin. Comments from users who can moderate comments aren't checked.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Find the HTTP status or symptom below. Errors and limits lists every error code. 400 Bad Request ¶ validation_error : message names the field. blog and user_ip are required, and user_ip must be the visitor's IPv4 or IPv6 address, not a hostname. invalid_json : the body isn't valid JSON. Send it with Content-Type: application/json and check the quoting in shell commands. 401 Unauthorized ¶ missing_api_key : send the key in the X-API-Key header. invalid_api_key : the key is mistyped, revoked or not a SpamAPI key. Keys start with spa_ ; Stripe keys don't work. Check the API keys page and create a new key if needed; the full key is shown only when it is created. If you also send api_key in the JSON body, it must be the same key as the header. 403 Forbidden ¶ account_unavailable : the account can't use the API. Contact support . 429 Too Many Requests ¶ rate_limit_exceeded : too many requests in a minute. Wait for the seconds in Retry-After , then slow down. See the rate limits . usage_limit_exceeded : this month's checks are used up. They reset at the start of the next UTC month; GET /api/v1/usage returns the time in resets_at . To continue now, upgrade on the dashboard's Billing page . 5xx Errors ¶ Retry with a growing delay, not in a tight loop. A retried check is a new check. Note the X-Request-ID response header for support. 503 Service Unavailable ¶ detection_unavailable means SpamAPI could not complete the spam check. The response contains no spam decision and does not use a check. Keep the submission pending for a later retry or manual review. Do not treat this error as a successful check or as a decision to allow the submission. quota_unavailable means SpamAPI couldn't read or record usage. Retry later. Every result looks the same ¶ Requests with is_test: true and user_role: "administrator" always return ham, and the test values always return spam, without classification. Remove them from real traffic. Send the submission's text in comment_content and the author details you have. A request with only blog and user_ip gives SpamAPI little to go on. WordPress plugin ¶ Connection failed: Invalid Key : paste the key again, click Save Settings , then Test Connection . The test uses the saved key. Connection failed with another message: the site couldn't reach SpamAPI, or SpamAPI answered with an error such as too many requests. Wait a minute and try again. Leave API URL at its default unless you run your own SpamAPI server, and check that the server allows outgoing HTTPS requests. Nothing is checked : Enable spam protection must be checked and saved. Comments from users who can moderate comments, pingbacks, trackbacks and unsupported form plugins aren't checked; see the supported comments and forms . Spam got through : if SpamAPI can't answer, the plugin lets the comment or submission through and writes the error to the PHP error log. This also happens when the month's checks are used up; the plugin's settings page shows the usage. Choose a higher Strictness Level to block more. A legitimate message was blocked : approve the comment from the spam list, or find the entry among the form's spam entries. Choose a lower Strictness Level to block less. Contact support ¶ Write to support@spamapi.de with the time of the request, the endpoint, the HTTP status, the error code and the X-Request-ID response header. Never send your API key.

docs.text: WordPress plugin setup ¶ The SpamAPI Anti-Spam plugin checks WordPress comments and the submissions of Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms and WPForms, without any coding. Setup takes a SpamAPI account, an API key and a few minutes in the WordPress admin. Before you start ¶ WordPress 6.4 or newer and PHP 8.3 or newer. A SpamAPI account: create a free account , or sign in . The Free plan includes 100 checks a month. An API key from the dashboard's API keys page. The quickstart shows how to create one. Use a separate key for each site, so you can revoke one without affecting the others. Use a current WordPress release receiving upstream security fixes. The plugin's minimum version is a compatibility floor, not a guarantee of upstream security support for older WordPress releases. PHP 8.3 receives security fixes through 31 December 2027 ; reassess the plugin's minimum before that date. Compatibility checks cover WordPress 6.4 with PHP 8.3 and current WordPress with PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. For newer PHP versions, use a WordPress release listed as compatible in the WordPress PHP compatibility table . Install ¶ Download the SpamAPI Anti-Spam plugin ZIP . In the WordPress admin, open Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin . Select spamapi-antispam.zip , click Install Now , then Activate Plugin . For a manual installation, extract the ZIP and copy its spamapi-antispam folder to wp-content/plugins/ , then activate it from Plugins . The download includes the PHP files, admin assets, and translations needed to run the plugin; no Composer installation is required. Connect your SpamAPI account ¶ Open Settings → SpamAPI and paste your API key into API Key . Leave API URL unchanged unless you run your own SpamAPI server. Click Save Settings , then Test Connection . It tests the saved key. “Connection successful!” followed by your plan, such as (free) , means the plugin can reach SpamAPI. “Connection failed” is followed by the reason; see troubleshooting . Under Enable SpamAPI , check Enable spam protection , choose a Strictness Level and click Save Settings again. Protection stays off until it is enabled and a key is saved. Configure ¶ Enable SpamAPI turns protection on. The plugin then checks WordPress comments and the submissions of every supported form plugin that is active. Strictness Level applies to all checks: Lenient blocks only obvious spam, Balanced (the default) blocks likely spam, and Strict blocks anything suspicious. Higher strictness may block more legitimate content. If SpamAPI can't be reached or returns an error, the comment or form submission goes through unchecked and the plugin writes the error to the PHP error log. The same happens when the month's checks are used up or the key no longer works. The settings page shows this month's usage. Supported comments and forms ¶ Source What's checked What happens to spam WordPress comments New comments from visitors, including signed-in users who can't moderate comments The comment goes to the spam list under Comments , where you can mark it as not spam. A SpamAPI column shows each result. Contact Form 7 The text of the form's multi-line fields as the message, plus the sender's name and email address Contact Form 7 treats the submission as spam: it isn't emailed to you, and the visitor sees the form's error message. Gravity Forms The name and email fields and the text of single-line, paragraph and post body fields The entry is marked as spam; you find it among the form's spam entries. WPForms The name and email fields and the text of single-line and paragraph fields The submission is refused, and the visitor sees “Your submission has been flagged as spam.” Pingbacks, trackbacks and comments from users who can moderate comments aren't checked. Contact Form 7 and Gravity Forms submissions that another spam check already caught aren't sent to SpamAPI and don't use a check. WPForms keeps no spam list, so a visitor whose message was wrongly refused has to reach you another way. Other form plugins aren't supported. Check that it works ¶ Sign out of WordPress, or open a private browser window, and post a comment or submit a form with the email address spam@test.spamapi.com . SpamAPI always classifies this test value as spam without using a check, so it should end up as described above. Then send a normal message to confirm that it goes through. Each checked comment or submission uses one of your monthly checks. Follow them on the settings page or the dashboard's usage page . Shared model contributions ¶ Shared-model participation is optional and disabled by default, for both free and paid accounts. Ordinary checks and legacy feedback do not opt you in. Test the connection in Settings → SpamAPI to retrieve the operator's published contribution notice, policy version and configured retention period. Read it, confirm your authority, visitor notices and any required agreements, then enable the separate Shared spam model setting. This setting alone does not establish every permission needed for visitor data. Server training availability defaults to on once the operator has configured the notice, retention and ledger; each installation still chooses its own participation. Configured sites with contributions off register a disabled installation in the background, including after a successful connection test. Once acknowledged, comment checks can use the shared model's canary scope without contributing labels. Registration leaves Shared spam model off and uploads no history. Explicit moderator spam, not-spam and reviewed approval actions can submit minimized comment text, language, opaque installation/item IDs, label and content revisions, timestamps and an authorized prediction reference. Separate author names, email addresses, IPs and request headers are omitted. Text and hashes can still contain personal data. These examples go to dedicated storage for SpamAPI's shared statistical comment model; they do not fine-tune a hosted AI provider. Moderation queues contributions locally and makes no network call. The queue is bounded to 1,000 records and a seven-day event age; retries use backoff and server retry delays. Budget waits do not exhaust transient-failure retries. Scheduled workers wake at the actual queued due time; expired content is removed even when an event is parked. Discarded events permit a fresh explicit moderation review. Permanent contribution rejections discard their rejected batch; transient outages, timeouts and budget waits keep the original events for retry. Settings show pending work and failure codes. On low-traffic sites, run wp cron event run --due-now from a real scheduler every minute. WP-CLI also provides wp spamapi training status , drain and retry . Historical backfill requires an explicit preview/confirmation; no history uploads on activation. Disabling participation atomically replaces pending work with a withdrawal control. Storage failures leave a repair marker that workers process before sending any superseded enrollment or label. Deletion withdrawals take priority and can replace unsent labels when the queue is full; deleted-item watermarks remain until an accepted withdrawal or global opt-out so a failed local write can be retried. Wait for the server status to show disabled before removing credentials or uninstalling. Deactivation/uninstall attempt withdrawal and clear local data; if offline or credentials are revoked, ask the account owner to confirm remote withdrawal. A failed submission is never reported as ingested. Models affected by withdrawal are retired or retrained; deleting examples does not automatically unlearn their influence. Continue using normal spam checks with contribution off. Withdrawals are delivered separately and remain available during collection pauses or policy changes. Site URL changes queue an authenticated rebind; checks continue while that update is pending. Old-site sources are withdrawn and contributor trust returns to quarantine after the move.
docs.title: WordPress setup

docs.text: The SpamAPI Anti-Spam plugin checks WordPress comments and the submissions of Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms and WPForms, without any coding. Setup takes a SpamAPI account, an API key and a few minutes in the WordPress admin.
docs.title: WordPress plugin setup

docs.text: WordPress 6.4 or newer and PHP 8.3 or newer. A SpamAPI account: create a free account , or sign in . The Free plan includes 100 checks a month. An API key from the dashboard's API keys page. The quickstart shows how to create one. Use a separate key for each site, so you can revoke one without affecting the others. Use a current WordPress release receiving upstream security fixes. The plugin's minimum version is a compatibility floor, not a guarantee of upstream security support for older WordPress releases. PHP 8.3 receives security fixes through 31 December 2027 ; reassess the plugin's minimum before that date. Compatibility checks cover WordPress 6.4 with PHP 8.3 and current WordPress with PHP 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5. For newer PHP versions, use a WordPress release listed as compatible in the WordPress PHP compatibility table .
docs.title: Before you start

docs.text: Download the SpamAPI Anti-Spam plugin ZIP . In the WordPress admin, open Plugins → Add New Plugin → Upload Plugin . Select spamapi-antispam.zip , click Install Now , then Activate Plugin . For a manual installation, extract the ZIP and copy its spamapi-antispam folder to wp-content/plugins/ , then activate it from Plugins . The download includes the PHP files, admin assets, and translations needed to run the plugin; no Composer installation is required.
docs.title: Install

docs.text: Open Settings → SpamAPI and paste your API key into API Key . Leave API URL unchanged unless you run your own SpamAPI server. Click Save Settings , then Test Connection . It tests the saved key. “Connection successful!” followed by your plan, such as (free) , means the plugin can reach SpamAPI. “Connection failed” is followed by the reason; see troubleshooting . Under Enable SpamAPI , check Enable spam protection , choose a Strictness Level and click Save Settings again. Protection stays off until it is enabled and a key is saved.
docs.title: Connect your SpamAPI account

docs.text: Enable SpamAPI turns protection on. The plugin then checks WordPress comments and the submissions of every supported form plugin that is active. Strictness Level applies to all checks: Lenient blocks only obvious spam, Balanced (the default) blocks likely spam, and Strict blocks anything suspicious. Higher strictness may block more legitimate content. If SpamAPI can't be reached or returns an error, the comment or form submission goes through unchecked and the plugin writes the error to the PHP error log. The same happens when the month's checks are used up or the key no longer works. The settings page shows this month's usage.
docs.title: Configure

docs.text: Source What's checked What happens to spam WordPress comments New comments from visitors, including signed-in users who can't moderate comments The comment goes to the spam list under Comments , where you can mark it as not spam. A SpamAPI column shows each result. Contact Form 7 The text of the form's multi-line fields as the message, plus the sender's name and email address Contact Form 7 treats the submission as spam: it isn't emailed to you, and the visitor sees the form's error message. Gravity Forms The name and email fields and the text of single-line, paragraph and post body fields The entry is marked as spam; you find it among the form's spam entries. WPForms The name and email fields and the text of single-line and paragraph fields The submission is refused, and the visitor sees “Your submission has been flagged as spam.” Pingbacks, trackbacks and comments from users who can moderate comments aren't checked. Contact Form 7 and Gravity Forms submissions that another spam check already caught aren't sent to SpamAPI and don't use a check. WPForms keeps no spam list, so a visitor whose message was wrongly refused has to reach you another way. Other form plugins aren't supported.
docs.title: Supported comments and forms

docs.text: Sign out of WordPress, or open a private browser window, and post a comment or submit a form with the email address spam@test.spamapi.com . SpamAPI always classifies this test value as spam without using a check, so it should end up as described above. Then send a normal message to confirm that it goes through. Each checked comment or submission uses one of your monthly checks. Follow them on the settings page or the dashboard's usage page .
docs.title: Check that it works

docs.text: Shared-model participation is optional and disabled by default, for both free and paid accounts. Ordinary checks and legacy feedback do not opt you in. Test the connection in Settings → SpamAPI to retrieve the operator's published contribution notice, policy version and configured retention period. Read it, confirm your authority, visitor notices and any required agreements, then enable the separate Shared spam model setting. This setting alone does not establish every permission needed for visitor data. Server training availability defaults to on once the operator has configured the notice, retention and ledger; each installation still chooses its own participation. Configured sites with contributions off register a disabled installation in the background, including after a successful connection test. Once acknowledged, comment checks can use the shared model's canary scope without contributing labels. Registration leaves Shared spam model off and uploads no history. Explicit moderator spam, not-spam and reviewed approval actions can submit minimized comment text, language, opaque installation/item IDs, label and content revisions, timestamps and an authorized prediction reference. Separate author names, email addresses, IPs and request headers are omitted. Text and hashes can still contain personal data. These examples go to dedicated storage for SpamAPI's shared statistical comment model; they do not fine-tune a hosted AI provider. Moderation queues contributions locally and makes no network call. The queue is bounded to 1,000 records and a seven-day event age; retries use backoff and server retry delays. Budget waits do not exhaust transient-failure retries. Scheduled workers wake at the actual queued due time; expired content is removed even when an event is parked. Discarded events permit a fresh explicit moderation review. Permanent contribution rejections discard their rejected batch; transient outages, timeouts and budget waits keep the original events for retry. Settings show pending work and failure codes. On low-traffic sites, run wp cron event run --due-now from a real scheduler every minute. WP-CLI also provides wp spamapi training status , drain and retry . Historical backfill requires an explicit preview/confirmation; no history uploads on activation. Disabling participation atomically replaces pending work with a withdrawal control. Storage failures leave a repair marker that workers process before sending any superseded enrollment or label. Deletion withdrawals take priority and can replace unsent labels when the queue is full; deleted-item watermarks remain until an accepted withdrawal or global opt-out so a failed local write can be retried. Wait for the server status to show disabled before removing credentials or uninstalling. Deactivation/uninstall attempt withdrawal and clear local data; if offline or credentials are revoked, ask the account owner to confirm remote withdrawal. A failed submission is never reported as ingested. Models affected by withdrawal are retired or retrained; deleting examples does not automatically unlearn their influence. Continue using normal spam checks with contribution off. Withdrawals are delivered separately and remain available during collection pauses or policy changes. Site URL changes queue an authenticated rebind; checks continue while that update is pending. Old-site sources are withdrawn and contributor trust returns to quarantine after the move.
